discussion_timeline.author: weisJ
discussion_timeline.body:
I am not quite sure why the previous setup for publishing didn't work out as I am not very experienced with the "raw" maven-publish plugin. I have now modified to use a setup which I know will work as I am using it myself. The following properties will be need to be provided locally (I recommend storing them in `<user_home_path>/.gradle/gradle.properties`:
- `ghGitSourceUsername`: The github user name. This is `gurkenlabs`
- `ghGitSourcePassword`: An appropriate github access token. It has to have access to create tags in the repo.
- `ghNexusUsername`: The username for the maven nexus you are publishing to i.e. `OSSRH_USERNAME`
- `ghNexusPassword`: The password for the maven nexus you are publishing to i.e. `OSSRH_PASSWORD`

For singing either of two approaches will work:
- Either
  - `signing.keyId`: The id of the gpg key
  - `signing.password`: The password of the gpg key
  - `signing.secretKeyRingFile`: Path to the gpg key
- Or:
  - `useInMemoryKey = true`
  - `signing.inMemoryKey`: The ascii armored version of the gpg key with `\n` instead of newlines (i.e. `OSSRH_GPG_SECRET_KEY`)

Then publishing works like this:
- For snapshots:
  ````
  ./gradlew prepareVote -Pgh -Prc=1 -Prelease=false
  ````
  Expected output:
  ````
  litiengine v0.5.2-beta-SNAPSHOT-rc1 is ready for preview.

  Git SHA: <some sha>
  Staging repository: https://oss.sonatype.org/content/repositories/null
  ````
- For releases
  ````
  ./gradlew prepareVote -Pgh -Prc=1 -Prelease=true
  ````
  Expected output is the same as for the snapshot version but instead a proper staging repository url (i.e no `null` path) and no `-SNAPSHOT` suffix.

In both cases an appropriate tag in the github repository is created.
The `-Prc=` property sets the version of the release candidate. It's perfectly safe to reuse the same number (I do this for snapshots to not clutter the the repo with tags). It will only affect the tag in the repo. For example in the above case the created tag will be called `v0.5.2-beta-rc1`.

In the case of releases (`-Prelease=true`) you still have to manually release it in the nexus repository manager. (I assume this is oss.sonatype.org for you.)

Please check whether this works for you as I can't test it myself :D

metadata.title: Add runtime DisplayMode switching with GUI rescaling

issue_payload.body:
## Context
`DisplayMode` (WINDOWED / BORDERLESS / FULLSCREEN) could only be configured before game startup — there was no way to switch modes while the game was running. Additionally, GUI component sizes were tied to the window dimensions at initialization time and were not rescaled when the window size changed.

## Summary
Wires `GameWindow` to respond to `GraphicConfiguration.setDisplayMode()` changes at runtime via a `ConfigurationChangedListener` registered in `init()`. The actual transition logic lives in a new private `applyDisplayMode` method.

**Key transitions handled:**
- **→ FULLSCREEN**: calls `gd.setFullScreenWindow(host)` via existing `prepareHostControl`
- **← FULLSCREEN**: calls `gd.setFullScreenWindow(null)` to exit exclusive mode before re-applying
- **→ BORDERLESS**: `prepareHostControl` now self-guards with `host.isDisplayable()` check and `dispose()` before calling `setUndecorated(true)`, covering both direct transitions and the FULLSCREEN→BORDERLESS fallback on unsupported hardware
- **← BORDERLESS**: `dispose()`, then explicitly reset `setUndecorated(false)` / `setResizable(true)` before `prepareHostControl` (WINDOWED path doesn't restore these)
- **Same-mode no-op**: `applyDisplayMode` short-circuits when `newMode == previousMode` to avoid redundant processing (since `ConfigurationGroup.set()` fires events even when old == new value)

A convenience `setDisplayMode(DisplayMode)` is exposed on `GameWindow` as a single call-site alternative to going through the config directly.

**Usage (either equivalent):**
```java
Game.window().setDisplayMode(DisplayMode.FULLSCREEN);
// or
Game.config().graphics().setDisplayMode(DisplayMode.BORDERLESS);
```

**Automatic proportional GUI rescaling on resolution change:**

`GuiComponent` now stores its position and size as fractions of the window dimensions (`relativeX`, `relativeY`, `relativeWidth`, `relativeHeight`) at construction time via `updateRelativeLayout()`. These relative values are recomputed whenever position or size changes through `setWidth()`, `setHeight()`, or `setLocation()`. On each resolution change, `onResolutionChanged(Dimension)` recalculates the absolute position and size from these stored fractions, so every component scales proportionally with the window automatically — no developer override required for basic proportional scaling.

For example, a button at `(100, 50, 200, 100)` on an 800×600 window stores fractions `(0.125, 0.083, 0.25, 0.167)`. When the window resizes to 1600×1200, it becomes `(200, 100, 400, 200)` automatically. The relative fractions are preserved across multiple resolution changes, so resizing back to the original resolution restores the original pixel values exactly (no floating-point drift).

**Per-component `autoScaling` flag:**

Proportional rescaling can be enabled or disabled on a per-component basis via `setAutoScaling(boolean)`. When disabled, the component retains its absolute pixel position and size across resolution changes. The resolution change event is still propagated to child components regardless of the parent's setting, so children with auto-scaling enabled will still scale even if the parent does not. Auto-scaling is enabled by default.

```java
// Opt out of proportional scaling for a specific component
myFixedSizePanel.setAutoScaling(false);
```

Game developers can still override `onResolutionChanged` at any level of the component hierarchy for custom layout logic that goes beyond proportional scaling:

```java
@Override
public void onResolutionChanged(Dimension resolution) {
    super.onResolutionChanged(resolution); // proportional rescale + propagates to children
    // custom re-layout logic
    myButton.setLocation(resolution.getWidth() / 2 - 100, resolution.getHeight() / 2);
}
```

`ScreenManager` lazily registers a `ResolutionChangedListener` on the first `add()` call and forwards all subsequent resolution changes to every registered screen, which then cascades through the entire component tree automatically via the inherited `GuiComponent.onResolutionChanged`.

## Additional thoughts
The `ConfigurationChangedListener` is registered at the end of `init()` (after the window is made visible), guarded by `hostControl.isShowing()`, so config changes before startup still take the normal path through `prepareHostControl` in `init()` without double-applying.

Switching to/from BORDERLESS requires a `dispose()` + re-show cycle — this is an AWT constraint and will cause a brief visual flicker on those transitions. This is unavoidable without a full OS-level borderless-window API.

`prepareHostControl` now defensively disposes the frame in its BORDERLESS case if it is still displayable (`host.isDisplayable()` guard). This prevents the `IllegalComponentStateException` that previously occurred when `setUndecorated(true)` was called on a displayable frame — notably when FULLSCREEN mode was unsupported and fell back to BORDERLESS internally, bypassing the disposal logic in `applyDisplayMode`.

Components created before the game window is available (e.g. in no-GUI test mode) fall back to setting their dimensions to the full new resolution on the first `onResolutionChanged` call, since relative fractions cannot be computed without valid window dimensions. In normal game operation, relative values are computed immediately at construction time and all subsequent resolution changes produce correct proportional scaling.

## Quality assurance
- [x] Wrote unit tests for new behaviour
- [x] Documented new code thoroughly
- [ ] Fixed issues that would be regarded as code smells by sonarcloud
- [x] Ensured integrity of the build pipeline

discussion_timeline.author: copilot-swe-agent
discussion_timeline.body:
> @copilot that works most of the time, but sometimes setting the display mode dynamically yields this:
> ```
> Mar 28, 2026 6:32:35 PM de.gurkenlabs.litiengine.DefaultUncaughtExceptionHandler uncaughtExc...

Fixed in `209daa3`. The crash happened because `setUndecorated(true)` requires the frame to be non-displayable, but `prepareHostControl` wasn't always ensuring this. Two root causes:

1. **FULLSCREEN fallback**: When fullscreen isn't supported, `prepareHostControl` falls back to BORDERLESS internally — but `applyDisplayMode` only disposed the frame for direct BORDERLESS transitions, not this fallback path.
2. **Same-mode re-set**: `ConfigurationGroup.set()` fires events even when old == new value, so re-setting the current mode could reach `setUndecorated` without disposal.

Fix: `prepareHostControl`'s BORDERLESS case now checks `host.isDisplayable()` and disposes if needed before calling `setUndecorated(true)`, covering all paths. `applyDisplayMode` also short-circuits when `newMode == previousMode`.
